summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was admitted with facial swelling and acute-on-chronic right upper quadrant abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a clot in the superior vena cava extending toward the right atrium, managed with Argatroban initially and transitioned to warfarin. Due to her history of HIT, heparin was avoided. Her abdominal pain was attributed to a Crohn’s flare, and she was treated with a non-allergenic antibiotic. Pain and anxiety were managed with Dilaudid, Oxazepam, and Benadryl. Her symptoms improved, INR stabilized, and she was discharged home on warfarin, Cipro, and adjusted psychiatric medications with follow-up arranged. No surgical intervention was required.
